rationale: I read the full held EO 14228 (90 FR 11463-11464): its only operative command (sec. 2) amends sec. 2(a) of EO 14195 to raise the IEEPA ad valorem duty on PRC products from 10 to 20 percent; no sunset or savings clause. I read the full held official FR text of EO 14389 (91 FR 9437-9439): sec. 1 provides that 'the additional ad valorem duties imposed pursuant to IEEPA in ... Executive Order 14195, as amended ... shall no longer be in effect', sec. 2(a) directs agencies to end them, and sec. 2(d) limits the order to those IEEPA duties; the national emergencies and non-duty actions are preserved, but EO 14228 has no non-duty content. The ACT: record's span was captured from an APP copy, but I verified the identical sec. 2(a) wording in the held official FR actor text ACTOR_TEXT:EO:14389, which is the text I rely on. Refutation attempt: I found in the held FR corpus EO 14357 (Nov. 4, 2025, 90 FR 50725), which expressly reduced the 20 percent rate set by EO 14228 to 10 percent effective Nov. 10, 2025; that is very probably the first end of EO 14228's operative content and the producer did not identify it (it records the first end as unresolved). That only moves the end earlier and makes the NO stronger; EO 14389 then ends whatever IEEPA duty remained under EO 14195 as amended. De minimis suspensions citing EO 14195 'as amended by EO 14228' concern the article class, which EO 14228 did not change. Independent view NO; I agree, with EO 14357 recorded as the likely first-end instrument for lifecycle work and later court rulings or reinstatements after Feb. 20, 2026 as unexamined. Nonauthoritative AI hypothesis.
